svg.text: struct state → methods → constructor/encapsulation → composition → interfaces → generics → project v.2

text.tspan: Fields combine different data types.
Use values, pointers, nested and anonymous fields.
Equality requires same type + comparable fields.
Uppercase names cross package boundary.
Struct stores domain state.
Method = function bound to receiver.
Value receiver works on copy.
Pointer receiver mutates instance.
Receiver type and method share package.
Behavior joins state at named type.
New / NewType = constructor function.
Can return value or pointer.
Package is encapsulation boundary in source.
Lowercase hides internals.
Validation is needed to preserve invariants.
Embed anonymous base-like struct.
Outer type gains promoted methods.
Same-name outer method wins lookup.
Source frames composition as inheritance substitute.
Explicit embedded access remains possible.
Interface = method declarations without implementation.
Concrete type satisfies method set implicitly.
Use as argument, return, variable or slice element.
Interface narrows visible behavior to method set.
Runtime polymorphism selects concrete implementation.
interface{} can hold different concrete types.
Assertion: value, ok := i.(T).
Type switch selects by dynamic type.
Interfaces may embed other interfaces.
Interface field enables swappable components.
Car example swaps IMotor implementations.
Type parameters reduce duplicate implementations.
any = unrestricted in source examples.
comparable = equality-capable type set.
Union constraints: int | float64 | string.
~int includes named types with int underlying type.
Generic functions and structs are demonstrated.
Do not expose fields/methods that callers do not need.
Do not put every structure method into one large interface.
Hidden fields still require validation in mutating methods.
Unchecked type assertion may fail at runtime.
Generic constraints must match operations required by code.
Board owns grid, moves, win/draw checks and rendering.
Player owns current figure and turn switching.
Game owns input, state and orchestration.
main constructs Board + Player + Game then calls Play.
Behavior from procedural v.1 is redistributed with minimal logic changes.
Exercises: Z player, restart, tests, reset-board command.

svg.text: Acceptance: explain struct/method receiver semantics, package visibility, composition, interface mechanics and generic constraints.
Project acceptance: map responsibilities to Board / Player / Game and explain v.1 → v.2 refactoring.
